note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) species-level description, the original in English. The original used the old combination Hamitermes (Ahamitermes) pumilus, now placed in Incolitermes. The original states 'Winged adult: Not known.', hence no alate section; a nymph (penultimate nymph) section is present. The original records the distribution only as 'New South Wales: Mt. Lindsay (near the Queensland border)' and does not label a type locality in that passage; the Unumgar State Forest recorded in the grouping checklist is a later refinement of that type locality and the lead should verify it.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original (Hill 1942) published it as Hamitermes (Ahamitermes) pumilus, known only from the type series (2 soldiers, 1 brachypterous neotenic reproductive, and many workers and nymphs), taken from the nursery cells and other galleries of a large nest of Coptotermes acinaciformis in the trunk of a living Eucalyptus paniculata at Mt Lindsay, New South Wales (near the Queensland border). The soldier is much smaller and paler than H. nidicola.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Penultimate nymph: compound eyes partly pigmented; mandibles as in Fig. 279; wing buds about 0.66 long; pronotum hemispherical, its shape distinctly different from that of the same stage in H. nidicola and H. hilli. Tibial spurs 2:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Much smaller and paler than H. nidicola. Most of the pronotum and head pale yellow, the vertex creamy white, the apex of the mandibles pale rusty, becoming dark orange towards the base. Head and thorax with sparse long straight hairs; antennae and legs with more numerous long curved hairs. Abdomen more sparsely and shortly hairy. Head (Fig. 280) slightly arched, distinctly longer than wide, widest at about the posterior third, slightly narrowed anteriorly. Labrum short, wide and strongly convex, slightly wider than long, slightly narrowed at the sides, very broadly rounded anteriorly, with sparse long hairs. Postclypeus strongly bilobed. Frons depressed, wrinkled, slightly darker than the rest of the head. Mandibles showing no trace of teeth, about half the length of the head capsule, far apart from each other at the base externally. Fontanelle very inconspicuous. Antennae extending beyond the apex of the mandibles by about half their length; segment 1 large, about half as wide as long, subcylindrical; segment 2 slightly narrower, less than half the length of segment 1, subcylindrical; segment 3 very small; segments 4—12 moniliform, about as long as wide; segment 13 slightly longer and narrower than segment 12. Pronotum more than twice as wide as long, slightly narrower than the head, nearly flat, the anterior margin slightly convex, the posterior margin slightly concave. Tibial spurs 2:2:2. Measurements: total length 3.60; head length (with mandibles) 1.13—1.24; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.69; head length (to apex of labrum) 0.97—0.99; head width 0.62—0.66; pronotum length 0.22—0.24; pronotum width 0.50.
